course_title: BIOL 97 Honors Research in Biology I
description: Original and independent investigation of a biological problem with associated study of primary literature sources under the supervision of a faculty member. Open only to Dartmouth Biology majors. Projects may include research in laboratory settings, field work, modeling, data mining, or development of new methodologies that will further understanding of a relevant basic or applied biological problem. Required of honors students as part of the major. Students takingBIOL 95andBIOL 97may count only one of these courses toward the elective courses for their major. In no case may a student elect more than two from courses amongBIOL 95, 96, 97, and 98. Students who have completed or are takingBIOL 97may enroll and receive college credit forBIOL 99during spring term of their senior year.Students are awarded one course credit for successful completion of this course at the end of the third term of study. 			<div id="main"><h1>
	<span>BIOL 97</span> Honors Research in Biology I
</h1><div class="desc">
	<p>Original and independent investigation of a biological problem with associated study of primary literature sources under the supervision of a faculty member. Open only to Dartmouth Biology majors. Projects may include research in laboratory settings, field work, modeling, data mining, or development of new methodologies that will further understanding of a relevant basic or applied biological problem. Required of honors students as part of the major. Students taking <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-95'>BIOL 95</a> and <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-97'>BIOL 97</a> may count only one of these courses toward the elective courses for their major. In no case may a student elect more than two from courses among <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-95'>BIOL 95</a>, 96, 97, and 98. Students who have completed or are taking <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-97'>BIOL 97</a> may enroll and receive college credit for <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-99'>BIOL 99</a> during spring term of their senior year.</p>
<p>Students are awarded one course credit for successful completion of this course at the end of the third term of study. Students subsequently register for <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-98'>BIOL 98</a> and continue with their coursework into a third term.  Students do not register for a third term. A final grade will replace the “ON” for both BIOL 098 and this course upon completion of this course at the end of the third term of coursework.</p>
</div><div class="sc_prereqs">
	<h3>
		Prerequisite
	</h3>At least two Biology courses numbered 20 or above, a 3.0 average in previous Biology courses, and permission of the Undergraduate Committee and the supervising instructor, obtained at least one month prior to the beginning of the term in which the course is to be elected.
</div><div class="sc_coreqs">

			<div id="main"><h1>
	<span>BIOL 98</span> Honors Research in Biology II
</h1><div class="desc">
	<p>Original and independent investigation of a biological problem with associated study of primary literature sources under the supervision of a faculty member. Open only to Dartmouth Biology majors. Projects may include research in laboratory settings, field work, modeling, data mining, or development of new methodologies that will further understanding of a relevant basic or applied biological problem. <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-98'>BIOL 98</a> does not count for credit in the major.  In no case may a student elect more than two courses among <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-95'>BIOL 95</a>, 96, 97, and 98. Students who have completed or are enrolled in <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-98'>BIOL 98</a> may enroll and receive college credit for <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-99'>BIOL 99</a> during spring term of their senior year.</p>
<p>Students are awarded one course credit for successful completion of this course. Students who have registered for <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-97'>BIOL 97</a> register for this course and continue with their coursework into a third term. Students do not register for a third term. A final grade will replace the “ON” for both <a class='sc-courselink' href='/en/current/orc/departments-programs-undergraduate/biological-sciences/biol-biological-sciences-undergraduate/biol-97'>BIOL 97</a> and this course upon completion of this course at the end of the third term of coursework.</p>
</div><div class="sc_prereqs">
	<h3>
		Prerequisite
